name: crash-reporting
description: Native + JS crash reporting behind a lazy app-owned wrapper, consent-gated, shipped dark until the Firebase config files exist.

notes: NATIVE module: dev clients and store builds must be rebuilt. The lazy require in lib/crash is what keeps binaries built BEFORE this module from crashing at app start — never convert it to a static import.

iOS uses static CocoaPods AGAINST the rnfirebase docs: $RNFirebaseDisableSPM = true + targeted modular_headers (see README). Firebase's CocoaPods distribution stops publishing new versions after October 2026 — a future Firebase upgrade is a real migration, deferred knowingly.
firebase.json ships ALL auto-collection off; the app enables at runtime from its own privacy switch after settings hydration.

placeholders.what: the Xcode target name and app directory
doc-comment references to the app's settings context and decision record

postInstall: Guarded FirebaseApp.configure in AppDelegate (only when the plist is in the bundle).
Run the adapted add_ios_build_phases.rb (guarded plist-copy + dSYM-upload phases).
Android: google-services + crashlytics classpaths; apply both plugins only when google-services.json exists.
Consent wiring: setCrashReportingEnabled(!optOut) after hydration and on every change; settings resets must preserve the opt-out.
ErrorBoundary recordError hook + dev-only Test crash row behind a confirm alert.
Prove ship-dark: iOS simulator build AND gradlew assembleDebug green with no config files.
Owner console steps: Firebase project + iOS/Android apps + drop the two config files + rebuild; then Test crash → relaunch → report visible.
Update the app's decision records and store-review privacy notes (new third party receives crash data).
